title: Map Your Visual Blind Spot
question: How do target-visibility reports relate to the optic disc, and what can a coarse screen map tell us?

data.prediction: Target reports may vary with eye condition and position. Looking at the cross keeps the target at a controlled visual-field location. No clear disappearance is possible in an uncalibrated small run.
data.design: Keep a comfortable fixed distance, device, zoom and gaze. Compare distinct positions and both-eyes coverage, retaining uncertain or unexpected reports. These test selections are synthetic software-review evidence, not a participant vision assessment.

answers.structure: My structure explanation uses synthetic student-report test selections, not a verified human vision result. Rods/cones detect local light; the disc lacks those receptors, but nerve fibers still carry output from other retinal regions. Current point positions, visibility and viewing contexts support only a coarse reported pattern. The target remains drawn even when a report says not seen. A both-eyes point must match side, spacing, screen context and reported fixation before interpreting its own appearance. Browser pixels are not calibrated retinal units; gaze and distance are not tracked. Other-eye coverage and visual filling-in differ. No exact boundaries, whole-field area, health result or population effect is established.
